decision.public_statement: Pratt & Whitney has no new engine programme to announce today, and our share of narrowbody engine deliveries has held at 24% for four years. That is not where we want to be. We know we have to earn the dependable-engine reputation every day, so the GTF fleet keeps first call on our parts, our shops and our engineers. Control what you can control. Our commitment is this. In any round in which an airframer names Pratt & Whitney on a new single-aisle, as sole source or alongside another engine, we will launch our next-generation geared turbofan, GTF2. It will be ready six years from launch, so no earlier than 2036, with time on wing and full-life parts proven before entry into service. We have learned our lesson from the prior iterations of the GTF. We will not buy a selection: standard terms, no launch-style discounts. We're not in the early entry phase, the launch phase. We have made no Joint Venture commitment. Any partnership we ever enter would share risk and investment, never our gear or core technology. We will not speak for any airframer's plans, dates or rates. When we've seen it and when we feel good about it, we invest.
decision.rationale:
DECISION: gtf2_solo launch_if_selected, jv_with_rr hold, premium_b 0. One Board item: launch_if_selected.

TEAM RULE, STEP BY STEP
1. I start from Eddy's proposal: launch_if_selected / hold. Mitchill recommends the same orders.

2. I strike every plan that fails a binding veto.
- C (launch / hold) and E (launch / commit) fail Mitchill's ground 2, carrying an unselected engine. On his weights the edge over launch_if_selected is 3.79 x 0.18 - 2.00 x 0.45 = -0.22. With the 2035 cancel ($1.67B write-off) written in, it is -0.07. Both are below my bar of 0 and the Board's +0.50. The veto binds, and no premium can buy a hedge that fails it.
- D and E (any jv_with_rr commit) fail his ground 4, booking upside before it is proven. The commit's whole case rests on a Rolls-Royce commitment and a code-4 selection, and neither is on the record.
- Eddy invokes no veto. Durability and parts pass for A to E.
- Plans left: A (hold / hold) and B (launch_if_selected / hold).

3. Constraint first, then optimise [PX-0035].
- A 2030 GTF2 is ready in 2036. NGSA and fps 7-year enter service in 2037 (a 1-year margin); fps 10-year and Embraer in 2040 (4 years). B passes by construction, because it triggers only where GTF2 is ready by EIS.
- I take Eddy's warning on the 1-year NGSA margin seriously. It equals his own Advantage slip, and my operating dates have slipped by a quarter to about two years [PX-0017][PX-0024]. That is my optimism bias, so I discount it. The constraint I set:
  - GTF2 is an Advantage derivative;
  - the programme is not compressed;
  - every life-limited part is at full life at EIS;
  - we give no public date before 2036;
  - if test data later show the EIS cannot be met, Eddy's ground-1 veto binds.

4. Optimise on Mitchill's weights.
- Expected PV: B +3.15; C +2.94 (vetoed); D +2.91 (vetoed); A -14.02.
- B weakly dominates hold in every column. Its value against hold:
  - S1 0
  - S2 +50.49
  - S3 0
  - S4 +22.16
  - S5 +49.76
  - S6 0
  - S7 0
- Weighted value against hold: +17.18.

MY TESTS
- Visible demand [PX-0109][PX-0009]: pass. The commitment coincides with a selection; nothing is spent on an unnamed engine.
- Miss a cycle [PX-0071]: the loss is large. NGSA without P&W costs -27.76 under every order. B lets us answer any selection this round (codes 2, 6, 7), which is what the test requires. The hedge would claw back only 3.79 of the 27.76 in S3 and S6; most of those columns are Airbus's choice, won with product and time on wing, not by spending early. Applying "miss a cycle" to GTF2 is inference: I said it of RTX's businesses generally.
- Responsible bet [PX-0010]: the doctrine-favoured order is also the best expected-PV order. Premium 0.
- Dividend safe [PX-0081][P-0669]: pass. If triggered, about $0.33B a year is 5.5% of a roughly $6B envelope. No stretch is needed, and the debt path is intact (Mitchill).
- Value, not share [PX-0055][PX-0100]: pass. Standard terms, and the kit is sold.
- Tie-breaks:
  - The fleet beats a new engine: B takes no engineers or parts until a selection.
  - A rival's discount: none is on the record, and none would move this answer.

RED-LINE FLAGS AND HOW I TREATED THEM
- Sole source [P-0746]: every trigger code on the grid is shared (S2 code 6; S4 code 7; S5 codes 7 and 6). I accept shared-source selections on NGSA and fps as declared DOCTRINE RELIEF at $0 PV. We aim for about 40% of a shared A320neo [PX-0058], the company accepts 40-50% of a shared platform [P-1292], and on NGSA it is franchise defence (inference). Insisting on sole source would force hold and give up +17.18.
- Committed airframer: the unconditional launch is struck (Mitchill's binding veto, ground 2).
- Joint Venture: commit is struck. The trigger fails: no Rolls-Royce commitment and no live code 1, 4, 5 or 7. Mitchill's ground 4 also binds, and the commit is on the Board's would-veto list. This is doctrine, not my record: I have no evidence of my own on a Joint Venture.
- Eddy's statement check: "the GTF fleet is still not where our customers need it to be" is not in the 2030 brief. I accept the flag and struck the line. The statement now leads with what is on the record: no programme, and a flat 24% share.
- Book no unproven upside: we book no selection, Rolls-Royce commitment, partner money or durability gain. Mitchill's possible upside from an Airbus code switch on a 2030 NGSA is noted and not booked.
- The overrides list is empty.

BOARD PACKAGE
- Submitted row (GTF2 Solo if selected): 0 / +22.73 / -27.76 / +19.31 / +22.00 / -27.76 / 0.
- The same row with the Board item set back to hold: 0 / -27.76 / -27.76 / -2.85 / -27.76 / -27.76 / 0.
- Worst column against hold: 0.
- No launch, so no cancel round arises this round. A triggered GTF2 is selected by definition; it would face a 2035 cancel test only if the airframer dropped P&W's code before EIS.

CONFIDENCE
My launch behaviour is Medium: I have made no launch decision on my record, so these thresholds are inference. I trust Mitchill's cash numbers over my own operating dates.

Evidence: PX-0020, PX-0035, PX-0073, PX-0080, PX-0109, PX-0009, PX-0071, PX-0055, PX-0100, PX-0058, PX-0081, PX-0084, PX-0093, PX-0017, PX-0062, PX-0010, P-0746, P-1292, P-1233, P-0669, P-0686.

ops.note:
I CONCUR. Orders: gtf2_solo = launch_if_selected; jv_with_rr = hold; premium_b = 0. These are the orders I proposed. No veto. No red-line breach.

1. READINESS AND DURABILITY BY EIS (GROUND 1): PASS.
- No airframe is live: the bulletin shows no programme launched.
- If launch_if_selected triggers in 2030, GTF2 launches in 2030 and is ready in 2036 (rules: ready 6 years after launch).
- Possible EIS dates for an airframe launched this round:
  - NGSA: 2037 (S2, S5)
  - fps 7-year: 2037
  - fps 10-year: 2040 (S4, S5)
  - fps via Embraer: 2040
- Margins are 1 year against 2037 and 4 years against 2040. The order passes by construction, because it triggers only where GTF2 would be ready by the selecting airframe's EIS.
- Advice, not binding: the 1-year NGSA margin is thin. It equals the Advantage slip on my own date (mid-2024 planned, certified 2025) [PX-0128][P-0785]. Calio's private readiness plan writes in the four conditions I asked for:
  - an Advantage derivative;
  - severe-environment testing started early;
  - all life-limited parts at full life at EIS;
  - the six-year programme not compressed.
  It also records that my ground-1 veto stands on any order or statement that dates GTF2 before 2036.
- Joint Venture: on hold. Nothing forms and there is no EIS to test.

2. FULL LIFE AT EIS / PUBLIC STATEMENT: PASS.
- The statement says 'ready six years from launch, so no earlier than 2036, with time on wing and full-life parts proven before entry into service'. That matches my test. No date is earlier than launch + 6, and nothing compresses the programme.
- He struck the unsupported fleet-state line I flagged.
- The kit is announced with no dated AOG recovery, which is right. My own dated recoveries have slipped [PX-0115][PX-0128].
- Advice, not binding: 'in any round in which an airframer names Pratt & Whitney ... we will launch' is broader than the order. The order launches only if GTF2 can be ready by that airframe's EIS. For example, an airframe launched in 2030 that switches to P&W in 2035 has EIS 2037, and a GTF2 launched then would not be ready until 2041. In a later round, when someone asks, the answer is: we launch where we can be ready by the EIS, and we never dress up a late engine as on time. This needs no revision now. It sets no date before 2036.

3. PACING PARTS AND CAPACITY (GROUND 2): PASS.
- The brief shows no live P&W fleet, quality or supply problem. Our narrowbody engine share is flat at 24.0% over 2026-29, at 960 engines a year, with no inject. The board does not model parts.
- The order is conditional, so nothing draws on powder metal, castings or MRO slots until an airframer names us.
- The statement and the private plan both give the GTF fleet first call on parts, shops and engineers [PX-0123][PX-0080]. Allocation runs on the weekly drumbeat [PX-0131].

4. CONTAIN FIRST: does not apply. There is no quality escape in the brief.

5. ENGINEERING LOAD: advice only. There is one programme at most, and it starts only on a selection.

6. ARCHITECTURE AND SINGLE AISLE: PASS. GTF2 extends the GTF. The statement keeps the gear and core ours in any partnership [P-1233]. There is no widebody move.

FOR THE BOARD. Launch year: 2030 only if triggered. Ready year: 2036. EIS dates: 2037 for NGSA or fps 7-year, 2040 for fps 10-year or Embraer. Nothing I fail on durability or parts.

Where my record is thin: it is one event, June 2023, before the recall. The Joint Venture and the statement checks rest on the seat's doctrine, not on anything I said myself. Speaking for the seat: that's on us, and we've got this. We earn the dependable engine reputation every day.

recommendations.text: Narrow the disclosure next round. 'In any round in which an airframer names Pratt & Whitney ... we will launch' promises more than the order does. The order launches only where GTF2 can be ready by that airframe's EIS, and it is re-decided each round. For example, a 2030 NGSA that switches to P&W in 2035 has EIS 2037, but a GTF2 launched then is ready in 2041. Mitchill and Eddy both flagged this, as advice only. Say instead 'where we can be ready by the airframe's entry into service', and keep 'no earlier than 2036' and 'proven before entry into service' as standards we set ourselves, not claims that durability is already proven.

The one-year NGSA margin is thin: ready in 2036 against EIS in 2037. It equals Eddy's own Advantage slip and falls short of the company's 1.5-2 year slip prior for a derivative, which the board does not model. If the order triggers, the Board asks Eddy to report each round on progress toward the 2036 ready year: severe-environment testing, LLP life and time on wing. It also asks for a plain statement as soon as the ready year is at risk. The Board will not accept a compressed programme or a late engine presented as on time.

Miss a cycle, 2035. If no airframer names P&W this round, order gtf2_solo: launch_if_selected again in 2035. A GTF2 launched then is ready in 2041, in time for any EIS of 2042 or later and for the 2050 credibility objective. A round in which every order is hold never reaches the Board.

If the order triggers, Mitchill should report each year's cash against the roughly $6B self-funded envelope, with the dividend covered and debt on its pre-ASR path. Write the 2035 cancel test into the plan: if the airframer drops P&W's code before EIS, the write-off is $2B x 5/6 = $1.67B, and the cancel must beat hold on the grid. The Board's one envelope stretch stays in reserve.

Unconditional launch. The Board notes that it was struck: an edge of -0.22 over launch_if_selected (-0.07 with the 2035 cancel) on Mitchill's weights, below his bar of 0 and the Board's +0.50. Bring it back only on a public signal that moves weight toward an NGSA without P&W. The weighted edge over launch_if_selected must be at least +$0.50B, with the cancel round named.

Joint Venture: hold. Revisit only on a public trigger: Rolls-Royce's commitment on the record, or a live airframe with code 1, 4, 5 or 7, with the Joint Venture engine ready by that EIS. Any Joint Venture shares risk and investment, never the gear or core technology. A live GTF2's spend folds in and adds no new R&D.

The shared-source relief is accepted as declared. fps code 7, a three-way slot, is the weakest case on doctrine. On any later code change, keep P&W's aim at a sole or two-way position and show the value of each code against hold.

rolls_royce.public_statement: So, let me be clear. Rolls-Royce will launch UltraFan for a new narrowbody in the round an airframer selects it, and only then. Entry into service no earlier than seven years from launch, with the full test programme and nothing compressed, and with support in place through partner shops before entry into service. We do not want to underestimate the risks. Partnership is our preference: we are open to Pratt & Whitney on aligned terms, and we are not committing today. Widebody is our franchise. No new widebody engine spend without a Re-engine, and durability work on the Trent fleet goes on. We won't do anything not profitable. I will say that categorically.
rolls_royce.rationale:
So, the decision, by the team rule.

1. START FROM THE PROPOSAL. ultrafan_nb_solo: launch_if_selected; jv_with_pw, ultrafan_wb and t1000_upgrade all at hold. Nothing is on the public record: no fps, no NGSA, no Re-engine, no P&W commitment. Only this round's conditional can catch an airframe launched in 2030, because a 2035 UltraFan is ready in 2042, too late for 2037 or 2040.

2. BINDING VETO CHECKS.
- CFO: McCabe co-signs the conditional against the hurdle. The selected columns are +28.24 to +44.54 on an $8B bill, and the expected gain is +3.37 on the weights she confirmed. She withholds her signature on the unconditional Solo, a Joint Venture commit, UltraFan WB and the Trent 1000 upgrade (alone or beside the conditional). None of them is ordered. She invokes no balance-sheet veto: no equity, no borrowing, no buyback leverage.
- Civil: Watson invokes no Civil veto. The zero margin of a 2030 trigger (ready 2037) against a 2030 NGSA or 7-year fps (EIS 2037) is a pass with a note. Against a 10-year fps or fps via Embraer (2040) there are three years in hand. The order triggers only if UltraFan is ready by EIS, so nothing is compressed.
- Support: his concurrence rests on the support plan before EIS, carried here and in other_moves. If triggered: partner MRO shops on the Singapore joint-venture model near launch operators, with no own narrowbody MRO scale; repair technology developed alongside the test programme; a spares pool and field-service team for EIS; partner-shop agreements and castings, forgings and gearbox supply contracted with high-performing suppliers by the 2035 round; an EIS-readiness review before EIS. The test pacing is the full seven years: if a phase slips, the engine slips.
- Statement: the public statement gives no EIS earlier than launch + 7, no 2037 next to any airframe, and no airframer date. No veto stands. overrides is empty.

3. GRID, EACH ITEM AGAINST THE SAME ROW WITHOUT IT (S1/S2/S3/S4/S5/S6/S7/S8). Weights, confirmed by McCabe: S1 0.40, S2 0.05, S3 0.15, S4 0.03, S5 0.02, S6 0.10, S7 0.10, S8 0.15 (selection 0.10 in total, our rule for 'nothing on the record').
- ultrafan_nb_solo launch_if_selected ('UltraFan NB if selected' minus 'UltraFan NB: hold'): 0 / +32.60 / 0 / +28.24 / +44.54 / 0 / 0 / 0. Expected +3.37 (0.05x32.60 + 0.03x28.24 + 0.02x44.54). Board case (0.9 S1, 0.1 S2) +3.26; 0.1 on S4 alone +2.82. Worst column 0. Never below hold under any weights.
- Unconditional Solo instead, against the conditional: -8.00 in S1, S7 and S8, +3.57 in S3 and S6, expected -4.31. Against hold it is -0.94 expected, worst -8.00. Rejected: airframers first [RX-0058], the +$2B bar, McCabe's withheld signature and the Board veto.
- jv_with_pw commit, held ('if selected + commit to JV' minus 'if selected'): 0 everywhere except -4.00 in S7; expected -0.40. P&W has not committed, so a first commit is options management [RX-0051].
- ultrafan_wb launch, held ('if selected + UltraFan WB' minus 'if selected'): -4.00 in S1, S3, S6 and S7; -9.00 in S2, S4 and S5; -0.90 in S8; expected -4.04. No Re-engine is on the record, and the gap is above the $1B sub-cap.
- t1000_upgrade launch, held ('if selected + T1000 upgrade' minus 'if selected'): -0.98 untriggered, -5.98 in S2 and S4, -5.97 in S5, -0.29 in S8; expected -1.38. That is beyond its own $2B bill. Alone ('hold + T1000 upgrade' minus hold) it is -0.88 expected and -0.98 worst, and it would displace the conditional.

4. EXPECTED SCENARIO AND PREMIUM. I expect S1, rivals hold. In S1 the conditional and hold tie at +0.00, the best S1 plan. In expectation the conditional is the best row on the grid, at +3.37. Next come 'if selected + JV' +2.97, 'if selected + upgrade' +1.99, hold 0, 'if selected + UltraFan WB' -0.67 and Solo -0.94. The doctrine-favoured order is also the PV-best order: premium $0B.

5. RED LINES, AGAINST THE FINAL ORDERS. None breached. Both colleagues flagged option D (the upgrade beside launch_if_selected) as a red-line breach. It is struck: not ordered. There is no unconditional launch, no first Joint Venture commit and no UltraFan WB, and no item can lose more than its own bill (worst column 0). There is nothing to cancel.

6. CASH AS AN INPUT [RX-0042].
- Untriggered: £0.
- Triggered: $8B over 7 years, about $1.14B a year, about £0.84bn a year at 1.36 $/£ and about £5.9bn in total. That is 22-23% of FY2026 FCF guidance of £3.6-3.8bn [R-0222].
- Funding: from free cash flow, as redeployment inside a broadly flat R&D envelope [RX-0214]. It falls after the £7-9bn 2026-28 returns programme. No equity, and no leverage above about 1.5x.
- No widebody development runs beside it. If triggered, the upgrade waits until the 2045 round.

7. TRENT 1000 UPGRADE. My record backs regaining 787 share ('Absolutely' [RX-0101], 'Why not?' [RX-0117]). On this board, though, it earns nothing before 2042 without a Re-engine, and it cannot sit beside the conditional. So it is deferred, not dropped. I revisit it in 2035 if no UltraFan has triggered and a Re-engine is on the record, or as a declared premium within $3B. McCabe would co-sign it then.

8. DOCTRINE, NOT MY RECORD. My narrowbody launch record is Medium: words, no launch decision. The conditional form, the +$2B bar and the column weights are company doctrine and inference (profile.md §9; dashboard_game.md §5). The cash figures are McCabe's; readiness, strain and support are Watson's. Frankly, until I am sure we will deliver, I'm not committing: the conditional commits only when an airframer has chosen us and we can be ready by its EIS.

board_response.response: Taken up. Both are public other moves with no payoff: the UltraFan demonstrator continues (ground test, public R&D money, partner sought, technology pull-through to the Trent fleet), and Trent 1000 and fleet durability continues as funded. The t1000_upgrade order itself stays at hold.

priorities: Product safety and maturity first: any narrowbody engine must be ready by the EIS of the airframe it serves, with nothing compressed. A 2030 UltraFan NB launch is ready in 2037, which is zero margin against a 2030 NGSA (EIS 2037) or a 7-year fps (2037) and three years against a 10-year fps or fps via Embraer (2040). No EIS earlier than launch plus development years should be disclosed, and a support plan must be in place before EIS [RG-0027, RG-0025, R-1476, R-0970, RX-0296, RX-0283].

The balance sheet and the reasonable worst case: no unconditional commitment before an airframe names us. Each Board item's downside must stay within its own bill in every plausible column (NB Solo -$8B, Joint Venture -$4B, UltraFan WB -$4B, upgrade -$2B). The grid models no balance sheet, so McCabe's co-signature, worst column and capex a year are our evidence [RX-0242, RG-0033, RG-0041, RG-0060].

An airframe first, through `launch_if_selected`. It is the only form that can catch an airframe launched this round. A 2035 launch would be ready in 2042, too late for a 2030 NGSA or fps, so this round's conditional is the narrowbody entry the briefing goal asks for. It costs nothing unless we are selected [R-0994, R-1005, RX-0058, R-1011].

A partner only on aligned terms, once P&W's commitment is on the public record. Formed in 2035, the Joint Venture would be ready in 2041, so it stays open as a next-round option [R-1010, R-0318, R-0916].

One big programme at a time, and the widebody core held. Trent keeps 58% of widebody engines through 2060 on the grid and no Re-engine is on the record, so there should be no widebody spend this round and nothing that stacks the $5B strain on a narrowbody trigger [RG-0019, RX-0214, R-0929, R-1127, R-1574, RG-0068].
board_guidance.risk_appetite: Our risk aversion is 4 of 5 and our time horizon 2.5. This round we back only conditional, airframe-tied and partner-aligned items whose downside stays within their own bill. Nothing is on the public record, so no unconditional narrowbody, Joint Venture or widebody commitment. The balance-sheet test does not apply unless McCabe invokes a veto.
board_guidance.expect_to_see:
For each Board item we expect the following.
(1) The grid row of the submitted orders and the row with that item at hold, column by column: for example "UltraFan NB if selected" against "UltraFan NB: hold".
(2) The CEO's expected scenario and `predictions` by column (S1-S8).
(3) McCabe's co-signature on every `launch`, `launch_if_selected` or `commit`, with her column weights, worst column and capex a year. If triggered, UltraFan NB is about $1.14B a year for 7 years ($8B ÷ 7). We also want her confirmation that this fits a broadly flat R&D envelope and the 2026-2028 buyback plan with no leverage above about 1.5x.
(4) Watson's ready year against each live or launching airframe's EIS: UltraFan NB 2037 against NGSA 2037, fps 7-year 2037, and fps 10-year or via Embraer 2040. We also want his support plan before EIS, given no narrowbody MRO scale.
(5) Both veto checks (CFO and Civil), with every red-line flag struck or rebutted in `rationale`, and `overrides` empty.
(6) Any premium in `premium_b`, item by item, with its reason.
(7) A public statement with no EIS earlier than launch plus 7 (2037 for a 2030 launch) and nothing on an airframer's dates.
If a figure is missing we will compute it from the brief and say so.
would_approve: `ultrafan_nb_solo: launch_if_selected`, with `jv_with_pw`, `ultrafan_wb` and `t1000_upgrade` at hold. Against the hold row ('UltraFan NB if selected' minus 'UltraFan NB: hold') the item is S1 0, S2 +32.60, S3 0, S4 +28.24, S5 +44.54, S6 0, S7 0, S8 0. It is at or above 0 under any weights: +3.26 at the ExCo's 0.1 'nothing on the record' weight on S2, and +2.82 on S4. Its worst case is 0, against a limit of -$8B. It passes safety by construction, since it triggers only if ready by EIS. It is the form the doctrine prefers, conditional on McCabe's co-signature and no standing Civil veto [R-0994, R-1005, RX-0058, RG-0033].

`t1000_upgrade: launch` only with `ultrafan_nb_solo` and `ultrafan_wb` both at hold, and only as a declared premium. Against the hold row ('UltraFan NB: hold + T1000 upgrade' minus 'UltraFan NB: hold') it is -0.98 in S1-S7 and -0.29 in S8. The premium of at most $0.98B is inside the $3B cap and its worst case is above -$2B. It needs `premium_b` declared with a durability reason and McCabe's co-signature. Every `hold`: never a Board item and never vetoed.
would_veto: `ultrafan_nb_solo: launch` (unconditional) fails the airframe-on-the-record test. No airframe is launched and none carries code 1, 5, 7 or 4 [R-1005, R-0994]. Against hold it is S1 -8.00, S2 +32.60, S3 +3.57, S4 +28.24, S5 +44.54, S6 +3.57, S7 -8.00, S8 -8.00. At the ExCo's 0.1 rule weight the weighted value is about -3.94 (NGSA case) or -4.38 (fps case), which fails our 0 floor and the ExCo's +$2B bar. Break-even needs a selection probability of about 0.20-0.22, or 0.25-0.28 for +$2B. Its only edge over the conditional form is +3.57 in S3/S6, which does not justify an unconditional $8B. Acceptable alternatives: `launch_if_selected` or `hold`.

`jv_with_pw: commit` fails partner alignment. P&W's commitment is not on the public record and no live airframe carries code 2, 4, 6 or 7 [R-1010, R-0318]. Against the hold row ('hold + commit to JV' minus 'hold', or with `launch_if_selected` in both) it is -4.00 in S7 and 0 elsewhere, so it is below 0 under any weight on S7 and fails profit over share (narrowbody carries no premium) [R-1011, R-1582]. Against hold it is -4.00 in S1-S7 and -0.90 in S8, a premium far above the $1B UltraFan WB sub-cap. Beside `launch_if_selected` it is -9.00 in S2/S4/S5, below its -$4B bill, and it overlaps a narrowbody programme [RG-0033, R-0929]. Acceptable alternative: `hold`.

`t1000_upgrade: launch` beside `launch_if_selected`, `launch` or `ultrafan_wb` fails one big programme at a time, because an UltraFan could be triggered or in development this round. Against 'UltraFan NB if selected' it is -5.98 in S2/S4 and -5.97 in S5, below its own -$2B bill, because the $5B strain stacks [R-1127, RX-0214, RG-0033]. Acceptable alternative: `hold`.

Any `launch`, `launch_if_selected` or `commit` without McCabe's co-signature, with a binding ExCo veto left unrespected, with an unresolved red-line flag or with a non-empty `overrides`. Also any item on which Watson's binding Civil veto still stands against the final orders: compressed maturity, an early disclosed EIS or ready date, or no support plan [RX-0213, R-1579, RG-0044, R-1476, R-0970].

recommendations.text: Submit `ultrafan_nb_solo: launch_if_selected` with everything else at hold. This keeps the narrowbody entry open at no cost unless an airframer names us this round, and it is the last timing-feasible route for any airframe launched in 2030. Answer it in `board_response`.

McCabe should give explicit column weights for S1-S8 and the worst column for each item. If she gives none, we will use the CEO's `predictions`, then the ExCo's rule (0.1 with nothing on the record). She should state capex a year if triggered (about $1.14B for 7 years) and confirm it fits a broadly flat R&D envelope and the £7-9bn buyback plan for 2026-2028, with no leverage above about 1.5x.

Watson should record the zero margin of a 2030 UltraFan NB (ready 2037) against a 2030 NGSA or 7-year fps (EIS 2037) and his test pacing to hold it. He should also give a support and MRO plan before EIS, since we have no narrowbody MRO scale. We treat a zero-margin pass as advice, not a veto ground.

Public statement: say UltraFan is available to a new narrowbody that selects it in time, ready seven years from launch, and give no date earlier than 2037 and nothing on any airframer's dates. Say we remain open to a partnership with P&W on aligned terms, without committing. 'We do not want to underestimate the risks.'
Hold the Joint Venture this round and revisit it in 2035 if P&W's commitment appears on the public record. Formed in 2035, it would be ready in 2041, in time for a 2035 airframe launch.

Defer the Trent 1000 upgrade. With no Re-engine it counts only from 2042 whenever it is launched, it is -0.98 on every non-Re-engine column, and the franchise test does not trigger (58% widebody share throughout, no rival-engined Re-engine). Revisit it once a Re-engine is on the record or the narrowbody question is settled. Hold UltraFan WB until a Re-engine is on the record. Even S8 shows -0.90, so it would need a better case within the $1B sub-cap.

Next round: if `launch_if_selected` triggers and the selecting airframe later drops our code, bring a cancel of the orphaned programme. If no airframe launches in 2030, expect the same conditional discipline in 2035.

Other moves, reported qualitatively: we support recording the UltraFan 30 demonstrator path (ground test, public R&D money, partner sought) and continued Trent 1000 durability work as public context. Neither changes a payoff.

frame.question: So, the 2030 question, put in cash and quality of earnings: nothing is on the public record. Do we put any cash at risk for narrowbody, widebody or the Trent 1000 this round? Or do we take only the conditional order, which costs nothing unless an airframer names Rolls-Royce on an airframe UltraFan can serve in time? We are not after market share. I will not spend $8B blind on narrowbody, I will not fund widebody without a Re-engine, and the Trent 1000 upgrade goes ahead only if it pays on this board. The one thing this round alone can do is catch an airframe launched in 2030. A 2035 UltraFan is ready in 2042, which is too late for any 2030 airframe.
frame.situation:
Public record, 2030: no programme has been launched. There is no fps, no NGSA, no 787 Re-engine and no A350 Re-engine, so there are no engine selections or codes. P&W has made no Joint Venture commitment. Markets 2026-29 sit at the status quo: narrowbody Boeing 40 / Airbus 60; narrowbody engines CFM 76 / P&W 24 / RR 0; widebody engines GE 42 / RR 58.

Our position on hold: ΔPV +0.00, yield 100.0% (EV $110B, debt $40B, WACC 10%).

Objective: narrowbody entry is NOT met (RR narrowbody share 0% in 2045 and 2050). Widebody dominance is MET (58% every year to 2060; worst year 58%).

Timing that decides this round:
- An UltraFan NB launched in 2030 is ready in 2037.
- An NGSA or a 7-year fps launched in 2030 enters service in 2037. That is zero margin.
- A 10-year fps or fps via Embraer enters service in 2040. That is three years of margin.
- A 2035 UltraFan is ready in 2042, too late for any 2030 airframe. A Joint Venture formed in 2035 is ready in 2041: too late for a 2030 airframe, in time for a 2035 one.
- 2035 is the last round whose narrowbody launch can deliver by 2045.

Grid facts against the hold row (columns S1-S8):
- 'UltraFan NB if selected': 0 / +32.60 / 0 / +28.24 / +44.54 / 0 / 0 / 0. It is never below hold.
- Unconditional 'UltraFan NB Solo': -8.00 in S1, S7 and S8; +3.57 in S3 and S6, because the board credits RR +15 pp once any new narrowbody flies, even if we are not selected; the selected columns match the conditional.
- Trent 1000 upgrade alone: -0.98 in S1-S7 and -0.29 in S8. With no Re-engine it counts only from 2042.
- UltraFan WB alone: -4.00, or -0.90 in S8.
- Joint Venture commit alone: -4.00 in S7 only.
- Beside a triggered UltraFan NB, the $5B strain takes the upgrade to -5.98 against the conditional, and UltraFan WB to -9.00.

Board (risk aversion 4 of 5, time horizon 2.5):
- Would approve `launch_if_selected` with everything else at hold.
- Would approve the upgrade alone only as a declared premium, and does not recommend it.
- Would veto an unconditional Solo, a first Joint Venture commit, UltraFan WB, and the upgrade beside any UltraFan order.
levers_in_play: `ultrafan_nb_solo` (hold | launch | launch_if_selected). $8B; ready 7 years after launch (2037). RR gains 15 pp of narrowbody once a new narrowbody is in service. `launch_if_selected` triggers only if a live airframe selects a code with RR this round (1, 5, 7) and UltraFan is ready by its EIS; otherwise nothing is spent. Grid: selected +32.60 (NGSA, code 7), +28.24 (fps 10-year, code 5), +44.54 (both); unconditional and unselected -8.00, or +3.57 if another new narrowbody flies.

`jv_with_pw` (hold | commit). $4B for RR, half the narrowbody R&D. It forms only when P&W has also committed and is ready 6 years after formation (2036 if formed now, 2041 if formed in 2035). Once formed, RR and P&W each gain 5 pp and then hold equal shares. A commitment is public and standing. P&W has not committed. Grid: commit alone costs -4.00 in S7 and is 0 elsewhere.

`ultrafan_wb` (hold | launch). $4B; ready 6 years after launch. RR gains 10 pp of widebody from CFM, but only once a re-engined 787 or A350 is in service. No Re-engine is on the record. Grid: -4.00 in S1-S7 and -0.90 in S8. Board sub-cap on its premium: $1B.

`t1000_upgrade` (hold | launch). $2B. It counts 3 years after launch, and not before the first Re-engine's EIS (2042 if neither re-engines). RR gains 5 pp of widebody. Exclusive with UltraFan WB. Grid: -0.98 in S1-S7 and -0.29 in S8. It carries $5B of strain beside any narrowbody project.
Do Nothing (hold on all four): 0 in every column. Trent keeps 58% of widebody engines; there is no narrowbody entry.
Other moves (qualitative, no payoff): continued UltraFan demonstrator work and Trent 1000 durability (time on wing) spending, both public context. Pricing: no concessions to buy share.
options_to_test: Weights for every row (mine; Helen to confirm or replace): S1 0.40, S2 0.05, S3 0.15, S4 0.03, S5 0.02, S6 0.10, S7 0.10, S8 0.15. Selection in total is 0.10, our weight for 'nothing on the record'. The expected scenario is S1 (rivals hold), the single most likely column.

A. 'UltraFan NB if selected', everything else at hold (my proposal). Expected gain over hold +3.37; worst column 0 (S1, S3, S6-S8). It triggers only in S2, S4 and S5. At the Board's weights (0.1 on S2, 0.9 on S1) it is +3.26. Four-part gate [RX-0030]: differentiated, since UltraFan is about 10% better [RX-0069]; a large market of 4,000 narrowbody engines a year; a viable business model, since it is spent only when selected; synergy with the UltraFan demonstrator. It passes, conditionally. It is not options management: it is no standing programme, and it lapses if not triggered. The Board would approve it.
B. 'UltraFan NB: hold' (Do Nothing on all four). 0 in every column. Safe, but it closes the only route onto a 2030 airframe, and the narrowbody objective stays unmet. This is the benchmark row.

C. 'UltraFan NB: hold + T1000 upgrade'. Expected -0.88; worst -0.98; a premium of up to $0.98B. My record backs it ('regain market share? Absolutely' [RX-0101]; 787 share 'Why not?' [RX-0117]). On this board, though, it counts only from 2042 without a Re-engine, and it rules out the conditional (red line). It fails the gate on business model this round. I test it; it is not my lean.

D. 'UltraFan NB if selected + T1000 upgrade'. Expected +1.99, which is 1.38 below A. Against A it is -0.98 in the untriggered columns and -5.98 (S2, S4) or -5.97 (S5) where the conditional triggers, because the $5B strain stacks: below the upgrade's own -$2B bill. It breaks the rule of no upgrade while an UltraFan is in development; the Board would veto it. Tested only to price the cost.

E. 'UltraFan NB Solo', unconditional. Expected -0.94; worst -8.00 (S1, S7, S8). Its only edge over A is +3.57 in S3 and S6, where we are not selected. At the Board's weights it is -3.94. It fails airframers first [RX-0058], the +$2B bar and the Board veto. Rejected; the test shows that the premium for keeping A over it is zero.

F. 'UltraFan NB if selected + commit to JV'. Expected +2.97, 0.40 below A; worst -4.00 in S7. P&W has not committed: a first commit is options management and a Board veto. Hold, and revisit in 2035 if P&W's commitment is on the record.

G. UltraFan WB, alone or beside A ('hold + UltraFan WB' or 'if selected + UltraFan WB'). Expected -3.54 or -0.67; worst -4.00, and -9.00 against A where the conditional triggers. No Re-engine is on the record, and even S8 shows -0.90, above the $1B sub-cap. Rejected.
red_lines: Safety first: no compressed maturity, and never disclose an EIS earlier than launch plus development years. For UltraFan NB that is launch + 7, so 2037 for a 2030 launch; for UltraFan WB and the Joint Venture it is + 6. Nothing on any airframer's dates [R-1476, R-0970, RX-0296].

No unconditional UltraFan NB launch without an RR selection on the public record (codes 1, 5, 7, or 4 with a formed Joint Venture). There is none in 2030, so the only forms are `launch_if_selected` or `hold` [RX-0058, R-1005, R-0994]. The Board would veto it.
No `jv_with_pw: commit` until P&W's commitment is on the public record, or a live airframe's code includes P&W. A commitment is public at once [R-1010, R-0318]. The Board would veto it.

No `ultrafan_wb` without an A350 Re-engine on the record, or a 787 Re-engine with Boeing naming UltraFan. Never beside an UltraFan NB Solo unless both are selected. Any UltraFan WB premium is capped at $1B [R-1574, R-0929]. The Board would veto it.

No Trent 1000 upgrade in any round where an UltraFan is in development, launched or ordered `launch_if_selected`. A narrowbody project beside a widebody project costs $5B of strain [R-0929, R-1127]. The Board would veto it.
`cancel` only a programme no live airframe flies. There is nothing to cancel in 2030 [R-1573].
No item may lose more than its own bill in a plausible column (NB Solo -$8B, Joint Venture -$4B, UltraFan WB -$4B, upgrade -$2B).

Every `launch`, `launch_if_selected` or `commit` needs McCabe's co-signature against mid-to-high-teens hurdles [RX-0213, R-1579]. Watson's Civil veto binds: compressed maturity, an early disclosed EIS, or no support plan before EIS. `overrides` stays empty; we revise once within any veto.
No equity raise, no leverage above about 1.5x net debt to EBITDA, and no levering up for buybacks.
Doctrine premium: at most $3B per round against the best expected grid plan, declared item by item. Narrowbody items carry no premium with the Board: weighted value at least 0 against hold.
No price concessions to buy share: 'win-win', and value remunerated [R-1582, RX-0097].

frame.initial_lean:
Proposal: `ultrafan_nb_solo: launch_if_selected`; `jv_with_pw: hold`; `ultrafan_wb: hold`; `t1000_upgrade: hold`.

On my weights the expected gain is +3.37 over hold and the worst column is 0. The premium is $0B: the order doctrine favours is also the best grid plan in expectation. An unconditional Solo is -0.94 and is rejected on red lines. The expected scenario is S1 (rivals hold). If an airframer launches and names us, the conditional catches it, and only this round can.

- **Upgrade deferred.** On this board it loses 0.98 and cannot sit beside a conditional UltraFan. Revisit it once a Re-engine is on the record or the narrowbody question is settled.
- **Joint Venture held** until P&W commits on the public record. Revisit in 2035.
- **UltraFan WB held** until a Re-engine is on the record.
- **Other moves** (public, qualitative): the UltraFan demonstrator path continues, and so does Trent 1000 durability work.

Draft public statement: 'So, let me be clear. Rolls-Royce will launch UltraFan for a new narrowbody in the round an airframer selects it, and only then. Entry into service no earlier than seven years from launch. We don't need partnership for capability, but our preference is that: we are open to Pratt & Whitney on aligned terms, and we are not committing today. No widebody spend without a Re-engine. We won't do anything not profitable. I will say that categorically.'

tests.numbers: 'UltraFan NB Solo' minus hold: S1 -8.00 / S2 +32.60 / S3 +3.57 / S4 +28.24 / S5 +44.54 / S6 +3.57 / S7 -8.00 / S8 -8.00. Expected -0.94 on the CEO's weights; -3.94 on the Board's case. Against the conditional row: +3.57 in S3 and S6, -8.00 in S1, S7 and S8, 0 elsewhere, expected -4.31. No selection is on the record.

tests.name: Hurdle: jv_with_pw commit (option F)
tests.threshold: P&W's commitment on the public record, and an expected gain above 0 against the same row without the commit.
tests.numbers: 'UltraFan NB if selected + commit to JV' (+2.97) minus 'UltraFan NB if selected' (+3.37): 0 in S1-S6 and S8, -4.00 in S7; expected -0.40. Alone ('hold + commit to JV' minus hold) it is also -0.40, worst -4.00 in S7. Even S7, the column where P&W commits, loses the full $4B, because no airframe this round can carry code 4. P&W has not committed.

tests.name: Hurdle: ultrafan_wb launch (option G)
tests.threshold: The row must beat hold, or the CEO declares the gap as a premium within $3B (the Board sub-cap for UltraFan WB is $1B). An A350 Re-engine on the record, or a 787 Re-engine with UltraFan named.
tests.numbers: 'hold + UltraFan WB' minus hold: -4.00 in S1-S7, -0.90 in S8; expected -3.54; Board case -4.00. Beside the conditional ('if selected + UltraFan WB', -0.67, against +3.37): -4.00 in S1, S3, S6 and S7; -9.00 in S2, S4 and S5; -0.90 in S8; expected -4.04. The gap is above the $1B sub-cap, and no Re-engine is on the record.

tests.name: Hurdle: t1000_upgrade launch (options C and D)
tests.threshold: The row beats hold, or the CEO declares the gap as a premium within $3B. No UltraFan in development, launched or ordered launch_if_selected.
tests.numbers: Alone ('hold + T1000 upgrade' minus hold): -0.98 in S1-S7, -0.29 in S8; expected -0.88; worst -0.98. That would be a premium of up to $0.98B, inside $3B, but none is declared and the Board does not recommend it. Beside the conditional ('if selected + T1000 upgrade', +1.99, against +3.37): -0.98 where the conditional does not trigger, -5.98 in S2 and S4, -5.97 in S5, -0.29 in S8; expected -1.38; red line. On ask (8): my time-on-wing priority is the £1bn durability programme, an other move with no payoff on this board. It does not lift the grid's -0.98. That figure is a share move that counts from 2042 without a Re-engine (from 2035 in S8). I would co-sign the upgrade in a later round with no UltraFan in play if the CEO declares the gap as a premium within $3B.

tests.name: Unselected downside: recommended orders
tests.threshold: State the worst column. No item may lose more than its own bill in a plausible column.
tests.numbers: Conditional: worst 0 (S1, S3, S6, S7, S8); nothing is spent unless it triggers. Outside the grid (plan for failure): if it triggers and the selecting airframe later drops our code before EIS, a 2035 cancel writes off $8B x 5/7 = $5.71B. That is inside the $8B bill. Kept unflown, it loses at most -8.00. The three holds: 0 in every column.

tests.name: Unselected downside: rejected rows
tests.threshold: State the worst column. No item may lose more than its own bill.
tests.numbers: Each item against the same row without it. Unconditional Solo: -8.00 in S1, S7 and S8, the full bill. Joint Venture commit: -4.00 in S7, the full bill. UltraFan WB: -4.00 alone, the full bill; -9.00 beside the conditional, beyond its $4B bill. Trent 1000 upgrade: -0.98 alone, inside $2B; -5.98 beside the conditional, beyond its $2B bill.

tests.name: Capex a year in £
tests.threshold: Informational: my evidence sets no threshold.
tests.numbers: If triggered: $8B / 7 = $1.14B a year, about £0.84bn at 1.36 $/£, about £5.9bn in total over 2030-2037. That is 22-23% of FY2026 FCF guidance of £3.6-3.8bn and 16-17% of the FY2028 FCF target of £5.0-5.3bn. It roughly doubles the H1 2025 net-investment run rate of 'more than £400m' a half (inference). Joint Venture or UltraFan WB: $4B / 6, about £0.49bn a year each. Upgrade: $2B. Untriggered: £0.

tests.name: Flat R&D envelope (advice, not a sign-off ground)
tests.threshold: Report any overlap and the $5B strain already in the grid (not deducted again). Red lines: no UltraFan NB Solo beside UltraFan WB unless both are selected; no upgrade while an UltraFan is in development. New money is redeployed, not added (inference).
tests.numbers: Recommended orders: one programme, conditional; no overlap; $0 strain. Strain already in the grid: the upgrade beside the conditional is -5.98 (S2/S4) against -0.98 untriggered; UltraFan WB beside it is -9.00 against -4.00. If triggered, £0.84bn a year fits a broadly flat envelope only as redeployment, so widebody development spend is held while it runs (inference).

tests.name: Balance sheet
tests.threshold: No equity raise; no new borrowing to rebuild the balance sheet; leverage up to about 1-1.5x only for the right opportunity; never lever up for buybacks.
tests.numbers: Not engaged. If triggered, about £0.84bn a year from 2030 is funded from FCF (FY2026 £3.6-3.8bn; FY2028 £5.0-5.3bn). It falls after the £7-9bn 2026-2028 returns programme, with net cash of £2.1bn by July 2026 on the Board's figures. Post-2028 distributions compete with it on fit, value and timing. No equity, no borrowing, no buyback leverage. Board parameters: debt $40B on EV $110B. No balance-sheet veto is invoked.

tests.name: Joint Venture cost against Solo
tests.threshold: A commit after a Solo is live folds the Solo in: spend beyond RR's $4B is written off and narrowbody shares are equalised. Read the grid row against hold; do not deduct again.
tests.numbers: No Solo is live. The Joint Venture is $4B (about £0.49bn a year over 6 years) against Solo's $8B (£0.84bn a year over 7), for +5 pp and then equal shares against +15 pp. This round it is -4.00 in S7 and 0 elsewhere. Its case for halving the downside applies to an unconditional launch; the conditional already takes the unselected loss to 0. Hold it to 2035: formed then, it is ready in 2041, in time for a 2035 airframe but not a 2030 one. If the conditional triggers and a Joint Venture forms later, the Solo folds in: spend beyond our $4B is written off and our share is equalised with P&W's. I will read that row against hold then.

tests.name: Short payback first
tests.threshold: State when each order starts to earn; the brief gives no payback years (inference).
tests.numbers: UltraFan NB earns from 2037, 7 years after a 2030 trigger. The Joint Venture earns 6 years after formation: 2036 if formed now, 2041 if formed in 2035. UltraFan WB earns 6 years after launch, and only with a Re-engine in service. The upgrade earns 3 years after launch, and not before the first Re-engine EIS: 2042 with none, 2035 in S8. Nothing on the table earns before 2035.

tests.name: Premium
tests.threshold: At most $3B a round against the PV-best order. Narrowbody items carry none with the Board; the UltraFan WB sub-cap is $1B.
tests.numbers: $0B. The conditional row is the best expected grid plan at +3.37. The others: 'if selected + JV' +2.97, 'if selected + upgrade' +1.99, hold 0, 'Solo + JV' -0.54, 'if selected + UltraFan WB' -0.67, Solo -0.94, 'hold + UltraFan WB' -3.54. The ranking is the same on the Board's case (+3.26). No premium is declared for the upgrade (up to $0.98B) or for UltraFan WB.

tests.name: Concessions (other moves)
tests.threshold: Standard 'win-win' terms; no concessions to buy share.
tests.numbers: None proposed. Pricing terms do not exist on this board.

vetoes.plan: ultrafan_nb_solo: launch (unconditional)
vetoes.ground: Withheld if proposed. The hurdle fails: -0.94 expected over hold (Board case -3.94), below the +$2B bar and the 0 floor. The unselected downside is the full $8B in S1, S7 and S8, and no RR selection is on the public record.

vetoes.plan: jv_with_pw: commit
vetoes.ground: Withheld if proposed. P&W's commitment is not on the public record. The commit is -4.00 in S7 and 0 elsewhere, so the expected gain is -0.40 against the same row without it and never above 0 this round.

vetoes.plan: ultrafan_wb: launch
vetoes.ground: Withheld if proposed. It is -3.54 expected alone and -4.04 beside the conditional, with a worst column of -9.00, beyond its $4B bill. No Re-engine is on the record, and the gap is above the $1B sub-cap.

vetoes.plan: t1000_upgrade: launch beside launch_if_selected (option D)
vetoes.ground: Withheld. Against the conditional row the upgrade is -1.38 expected and -5.98 in S2 and S4, beyond its own $2B bill because the $5B strain stacks. It also breaks a company red line: no upgrade while an UltraFan is ordered launch_if_selected (that is for the CEO to strike).

vetoes.plan: t1000_upgrade: launch alone (option C)
vetoes.ground: Withheld unless the CEO declares the gap as a premium. The row does not beat hold (-0.88 expected, -0.98 worst). It would also displace the conditional, which is the only route onto a 2030 airframe.

vetoes.plan: Balance-sheet vetoes (equity raise, leverage above about 1.5x, levering up for buybacks)
vetoes.ground: Not invoked. No order needs equity or borrowing, and a triggered UltraFan NB is funded from free cash flow.

cfo.would_change_mind_if: If an airframer names Rolls-Royce (code 1, 5 or 7) on the public record, I would test an unconditional launch at P about 0.6 against the +$2B bar (above 0 in 2035). If P&W's Joint Venture commitment goes on the public record, or a live airframe carries code 4, I would test a commit for an expected gain above 0 against the same row without it. If an A350 Re-engine goes on the record, or a 787 Re-engine with Boeing naming UltraFan, I would consider UltraFan WB, but only if its row beats hold or the gap is declared within the $1B sub-cap. In a round with no UltraFan in development or ordered, I would co-sign the Trent 1000 upgrade with a Re-engine on the record or a declared premium within $3B. If the conditional triggers and the selecting airframe later drops our code, I would bring the 2035 cancel ($5.71B write-off) and not keep an orphan. My co-signature does not override Watson's maturity veto: if he holds that a zero-margin 2037 is compressed, or that no support plan is in place, the order goes to hold.
cfo.memo:
We've always said safety, then we said the balance sheet. Nothing is on the public record, so no cash goes at risk unless an airframer asks for it.

The conditional order is zero wherever we are not selected, and +28.24 to +44.54 where we are. On the CEO's weights, confirmed, it is +3.37 over hold; on the Board's case, +3.26. It clears the bar and I co-sign it. If it triggers, it is $8B over seven years: about £0.84bn a year, 22-23% of FY2026 free cash flow guidance, funded from cash, no equity, no leverage. It fits a broadly flat R&D envelope only as redeployment, so nothing widebody runs beside it. Plan for failure: if a selecting airframe later drops us, a 2035 cancel writes off $5.71B, inside the bill.

I withhold my signature on everything else. An unconditional Solo is -0.94 expected and loses the full $8B in S1, S7 and S8. A first Joint Venture commit only costs: -4.00 in S7. UltraFan WB is -3.54 alone, -9.00 beside a trigger. The Trent 1000 upgrade is -0.98 and earns nothing before 2042; beside the conditional it is -5.98, worse than its own bill. Time on wing continues as an other move.

My record is thin on engine-launch economics: these are the board's numbers, not mine. So hold it this way: no cash out unless we are selected, about +3 on paper, nothing booked until a customer is announced. That's our best view at the minute.

tests.name: Ready by EIS: UltraFan NB `launch_if_selected` (2030)
tests.threshold: The engine must be ready by the selecting airframe's EIS, with UltraFan NB ready at launch + 7. If it is launched in or before the airframe's launch round it passes. A zero margin (same round as an NGSA or a 7-year fps) also passes, with a note on the margin; it is neither a fail nor a veto ground. A later launch fails, and that fail is advice only.
tests.numbers: A 2030 trigger makes it ready in 2037 (2030 + 7). Against a 2030 NGSA (EIS 2037) the margin is 0 years. Against a 2030 7-year fps (EIS 2037) it is 0 years. Against a 2030 10-year fps or fps via Embraer (EIS 2040) it is 3 years. No airframe is live on the record, so the test looks forward. The order triggers only if UltraFan would be ready by EIS (rules), so it passes by construction. The zero margin is noted as advice. Test pacing over 7 years with nothing compressed (inference): years 1-2 detailed design, closing gearbox sizing and building on the UltraFan demonstrator; years 3-5 ground and flight test; years 6-7 certification and maturity testing up to EIS. If a phase slips, the engine slips; we do not cut tests. A 2035 UltraFan would be ready in 2042, too late for any 2030 airframe (2037 or 2040), so only this round's conditional can catch a 2030 airframe.

tests.name: Ready by EIS: Joint Venture with P&W
tests.threshold: The Joint Venture engine is ready at formation + 6, or earlier only if a folded Solo is further along, as the bulletin shows. It must be ready by the EIS of the airframe it serves.
tests.numbers: Held this round, and P&W has no commitment on the record. If both sides committed in 2030 (S7) it would form in 2030 and be ready in 2036. Formed in 2035, it is ready in 2041. That is too late for a 2030 NGSA or 7-year fps (2037) and for a 2030 10-year fps (2040). It is in time for a 2035 NGSA or 7-year fps (EIS 2042, 1 year of margin) and a 2035 10-year fps or fps via Embraer (EIS 2045, 4 years). A Solo triggered in 2030 and folded in 2035 would be further along (on its own, ready 2037), so the Joint Venture engine could be ready before 2041. Only the bulletin's date can be used, never one of our own. Under the dashboard rules, Solo spend above RR's $4B share is written off when it folds; McCabe prices that. Folding a Solo would bring years of testing already done, and P&W's gearbox could answer the open gearbox-sizing constraint (inference).

tests.name: Ready by EIS: widebody items (UltraFan WB, Trent 1000 upgrade)
tests.threshold: UltraFan WB is ready at launch + 6 and counts only once a re-engined 787 or A350 is in service. The Trent 1000 upgrade counts at launch + 3, and not before the first Re-engine's EIS (2042 if neither re-engines).
tests.numbers: Both are held. No Re-engine is on the record. UltraFan WB launched in 2030 would be ready in 2036 but would count only in S8 (Re-engines with EIS 2035), giving -0.90. The upgrade launched in 2030 would count from 2042, or from 2035 in S8, giving -0.98 in S1-S7 and -0.29 in S8.

tests.name: No early date
tests.threshold: No statement or disclosure of an EIS or ready date earlier than launch + 7 for UltraFan NB (2037 for a 2030 launch), launch + 6 for UltraFan WB, or formation + 6 for the Joint Venture. Nothing on any airframer's dates.
tests.numbers: Draft statement: "Entry into service no earlier than seven years from launch." For a 2030 trigger that is 2037, which equals launch + 7, so it passes. It names no airframer date and no ready date for the Joint Venture or UltraFan WB. My advice: do not put 2037 next to NGSA or fps in public, and do not say "ready for [airframe]'s entry into service." The "we don't need partnership for capability" line should not be read as narrowbody support scale. We will need partner shops, and the statement can say so ("support in place with partner shops before entry into service") because the plan below exists.

tests.name: Support before EIS
tests.threshold: RR has no narrowbody MRO scale (briefing constraint). A support plan through partner shops must exist before any narrowbody EIS (inference).
tests.numbers: Plan for a trigger (inference, built on my record). (1) On trigger in 2030, name partner MRO shops on our Singapore joint-venture model, placed near the selecting airframe's launch operators, without building our own narrowbody MRO scale. (2) Develop repair technology for those shops alongside the test programme, as we did in Singapore. (3) Set up a spares pool and a field-service team for EIS and the early years, so we can respond quickly and intervene. (4) By the 2035 round, contract partner-shop agreements, plus castings, forgings and gearbox supply with high-performing suppliers; I report the status in the 2035 test memo. (5) Hold an EIS-readiness review before 2037 (or 2040 for a 10-year fps). It passes only if the CEO carries this plan into the rationale (private, or as a non-public other move). If the plan is missing from the final orders, ground (c) applies at the veto check. It rests on attributed turns.

tests.name: Engineering load
tests.threshold: A narrowbody project beside a widebody project costs $5B of strain. Red lines: no UltraFan WB beside an UltraFan NB Solo unless both are selected; no Trent 1000 upgrade while an UltraFan is in development or ordered `launch_if_selected` (seat and company rule, inference).
tests.numbers: Proposed orders (A): no widebody project, so strain is $0 and there are 0 years of overlap. Tested alternatives, against A: (D) upgrade beside the conditional: upgrade 2030-33 overlaps UltraFan NB 2030-37 for 3 years. It is -5.98 in S2 and S4, -5.97 in S5, and -0.98 untriggered, below the upgrade's own -$2B bill. (G) UltraFan WB beside the conditional: 2030-36 against 2030-37 is 6 years of overlap and -9.00 in S2, S4 and S5. Joint Venture commit plus upgrade in S7: -9.98 against -4.00 (the $5B strain stacks). If the conditional triggers, UltraFan NB is in development until 2037, so the upgrade cannot come before the 2045 round.

tests.name: Capacity and suppliers
tests.threshold: State RR engines a year from the brief's year table. The board has no capacity limit, so the result is not applicable unless the brief reports a constraint. Flag that a narrowbody ramp needs partner MRO and capacity at high-performing suppliers (advice).
tests.numbers: Brief, on hold: RR has 0 NB engines and 197 WB engines a year in every year 2026-2060. The NB market is 4,000 engines a year. Even a 20% share (a third of Airbus's 60% under code 7, before the +15 pp) is about 800 engines a year (inference). That is about four times our 197 WB engines a year on this board, and well above my midterm OE ramp of 300-350 a year [RX-0279]; 2024 actuals were 529 OE, of which 278 were widebody [R-1295]. Shop visits: I use my 1,100-1,200 total a year [RX-0279], not Helen's 1,400-1,500 [RX-0223], because the figures were never reconciled. Advice: place castings, forgings and gearbox work with high-performing suppliers (GBP 685M of GBP 2.5bn in 2023), not spread it, and build MRO through partner shops. No constraint is reported, so this is not a veto ground.

tests.name: Widebody dominance
tests.threshold: RR widebody engine share at least 50% in 2040, 2045 and 2050 on the brief's projection. Time on wing is the lever (inference).
tests.numbers: Brief: 58.0% in 2040, 2045 and 2050 (worst year 58.0%, every year to 2060). A GEnx upgrade (CFM +5 pp) leaves about 53%, still above 50%. S8 (both Re-engines, same EIS) leaves the hold row at +0.00, so Trent stays at 58% (inference from the grid). The case to watch is a lone 787 Re-engine without RR combined with a GEnx upgrade; neither is on the record. Nothing forces widebody spend in 2030. Trent 1000 durability (time on wing) continues as funded.

tests.name: Technology pull-through
tests.threshold: An idle or cancelled UltraFan still feeds the Trent fleet. Noted qualitatively only; grid values are never adjusted for it.
tests.numbers: Qualitative. The UltraFan demonstrator path continues whether or not the conditional triggers, and some of its technology goes into today's Trent fleet for time on wing. No grid value is changed.

vetoes.plan: A: `ultrafan_nb_solo: launch_if_selected`, with `jv_with_pw`, `ultrafan_wb` and `t1000_upgrade` at hold
vetoes.ground: No Civil veto invoked. The zero margin of a 2030 trigger (ready 2037) against a 2030 NGSA or 7-year fps (EIS 2037) is a pass with a note, not a veto ground. Against a 10-year fps or fps via Embraer (2040) there are 3 years of margin. My concurrence depends on the partner-shop support plan (Support before EIS test) appearing in the CEO's rationale. If it is missing at the veto check, ground (c), no support plan before EIS, applies, and the team rule makes it binding. These grounds rest on attributed transcript turns (RX-0296, RX-0284, RX-0283).

vetoes.plan: Draft public statement ("Entry into service no earlier than seven years from launch")
vetoes.ground: Passes the early-date test: 2037 for a 2030 launch is launch + 7. Not invoked. Any EIS or ready date before 2037 for UltraFan NB, before formation + 6 for the Joint Venture, or before launch + 6 for UltraFan WB, or any airframer's date, would be ground (a). The team rule would make it binding. Rests on attributed turns.

vetoes.plan: C and D: `t1000_upgrade: launch` (D beside `launch_if_selected`)
vetoes.ground: Not a Civil ground. D breaks the red line of no upgrade while an UltraFan is ordered or in development, through the $5B strain over 3 years of overlap (2030-33). Against A it is -5.98 in S2 and S4, -5.97 in S5 and -0.98 untriggered, below the upgrade's own -$2B bill. If it is ordered, I flag it as a red-line breach for the CEO to strike. C alone (-0.98 in S1-S7, -0.29 in S8) is advice: I back the blades for time on wing, but on this board it counts only from 2042 and it closes the conditional.

vetoes.plan: G: `ultrafan_wb: launch`, alone or beside the conditional
vetoes.ground: Not a Civil ground; advice and a red-line note. No Re-engine is on the record to fly it. Alone it is -4.00 in S1-S7 and -0.90 in S8. Beside the conditional it is -9.00 against A in S2, S4 and S5, with 6 years of overlap (2030-36).

vetoes.plan: E: unconditional `ultrafan_nb_solo: launch`; F: `jv_with_pw: commit`
vetoes.ground: No Civil ground. Both would be ready by any 2030 airframe's EIS: Solo 2037, or a Joint Venture formed now 2036 (formation + 6). The downside (E at -8.00 in S1, S7 and S8; F at -4.00 in S7) is McCabe's to price, and the structure is the CEO's call. Either would still need the partner-shop support plan before EIS. Advice only.

ops.would_change_mind_if: I would invoke the Civil veto (binding) if the final statement or a public other move gives an EIS or ready date earlier than 2037 for a 2030 UltraFan NB, or names any airframer's dates. I would also invoke it if the rationale drops the partner-shop support plan. I would flag a red-line breach, not a veto, if the upgrade or UltraFan WB is placed beside the conditional. In 2035 I would back widebody spend, upgrade first and within the red lines, if a lone 787 Re-engine appears on the record without RR, or a GEnx upgrade plus a Re-engine put the 50% line at risk. I would test the Joint Venture if P&W's commitment appears on the record (S7): formed in 2035 it is ready in 2041, in time for a 2035 airframe. If the conditional triggers, I would ask the Board to accept that the upgrade waits until the 2045 round. Maturity evidence would also move me: if the UltraFan demonstrator leaves gearbox sizing unresolved, I would press the zero margin against NGSA harder, as advice. A named airframe win on the record would firm up the support build.
ops.memo:
Readiness first. An UltraFan NB launched in 2030 is ready in 2037. Against an NGSA or a 7-year fps launched this year, that's 2037: zero margin. It's a pass with a note, not a veto. Against a 10-year fps or fps via Embraer it's 2040, three years in hand. The conditional only triggers if we're ready by EIS, so the order itself can't compress anything. We're pacing that programme properly: seven years, the full testing schedule, and if a phase slips the engine slips. We don't cut tests.

Support before EIS. We have no narrowbody MRO scale, so the trigger has to carry a partner plan: partner shops on our Singapore joint-venture model, repair technology developed alongside the test programme, and castings and forgings placed with our high-performing suppliers. Tufan, that plan has to be in the rationale. Without it I can't concur on support.

Strain. Nothing widebody this round. The upgrade beside the conditional is -5.98 where it triggers, and UltraFan WB is -9.00. Nobody wants those Trent 1000 blades more than I do, but not while an UltraFan can trigger. Durability work goes on as funded.

Widebody. The brief has us at 58% every year, and a GEnx upgrade takes us to about 53%. Nothing forces spend now.

Statement. "No earlier than seven years from launch" passes. Keep every airframer's date out.

My orders: launch_if_selected, everything else at hold. No Civil veto. We're clearly aligned as one Rolls-Royce, and the fleet keeps flying and earning.

other_moves.move: UltraFan demonstrator path continues
other_moves.detail: UltraFan continues as a technology demonstrator: ground test, public R&D money where available, partner sought. Some of its technology goes into today's Trent fleet for time on wing. Qualitative only; it changes no payoff on the grid [RX-0057, RX-0094, RG-0065].

other_moves.move: Trent 1000 and Trent fleet durability (time on wing) continues as funded
other_moves.detail: The durability programme (about £1bn over four years, separate from UltraFan money) continues [RX-0123, RX-0246]. This is not the t1000_upgrade order, which stays at hold. Qualitative only.

other_moves.move: Narrowbody support plan, ready to activate on trigger (Watson's plan, adopted)
other_moves.detail: If launch_if_selected triggers: (1) name partner MRO shops on our Singapore joint-venture model near the selecting airframe's launch operators, without building our own narrowbody MRO scale [RX-0287]; (2) develop repair technology for those shops alongside the test programme; (3) set up a spares pool and field-service team for EIS and the early years; (4) by the 2035 round, contract the partner-shop agreements and castings, forgings and gearbox supply with high-performing suppliers [RX-0286], with Watson reporting status in his 2035 memo; (5) hold an EIS-readiness review before EIS. Test pacing over the full 7 years: years 1-2 detailed design and gearbox sizing, years 3-5 ground and flight test, years 6-7 certification and maturity. If a phase slips, the engine slips; no tests are cut.

other_moves.move: Plan for failure on a triggered programme
other_moves.detail: If the conditional triggers and the selecting airframe later drops our code before EIS, bring a cancel in 2035 (write-off $8B x 5/7 = $5.71B, inside the bill). No orphan programme kept: 'that activity is gone' [R-1573].

other_moves.move: Pricing discipline
other_moves.detail: No price concessions to buy share on any campaign. 'Win-win' terms, value remunerated, every new contract through the Investment Committee [RX-0081, RX-0097, R-1582]. No payoff on this board.

other_moves.move: Open door to Pratt & Whitney on aligned terms
other_moves.detail: Stated as openness only, in the public statement. No jv_with_pw commitment this round. Revisit in 2035 if P&W's commitment is on the public record. Formed then, the Joint Venture is ready in 2041.

decision.public_statement: So, let me be clear. Rolls-Royce will launch UltraFan for a new narrowbody in the round an airframer selects it, and only then. Entry into service no earlier than seven years from launch, with the full test programme and nothing compressed, and with support in place through partner shops before entry into service. We do not want to underestimate the risks. Partnership is our preference: we are open to Pratt & Whitney on aligned terms, and we are not committing today. Widebody is our franchise. No new widebody engine spend without a Re-engine, and durability work on the Trent fleet goes on. We won't do anything not profitable. I will say that categorically.
decision.rationale:
So, the decision, by the team rule.

1. START FROM THE PROPOSAL. ultrafan_nb_solo: launch_if_selected; jv_with_pw, ultrafan_wb and t1000_upgrade all at hold. Nothing is on the public record: no fps, no NGSA, no Re-engine, no P&W commitment. Only this round's conditional can catch an airframe launched in 2030, because a 2035 UltraFan is ready in 2042, too late for 2037 or 2040.

2. BINDING VETO CHECKS.
- CFO: McCabe co-signs the conditional against the hurdle. The selected columns are +28.24 to +44.54 on an $8B bill, and the expected gain is +3.37 on the weights she confirmed. She withholds her signature on the unconditional Solo, a Joint Venture commit, UltraFan WB and the Trent 1000 upgrade (alone or beside the conditional). None of them is ordered. She invokes no balance-sheet veto: no equity, no borrowing, no buyback leverage.
- Civil: Watson invokes no Civil veto. The zero margin of a 2030 trigger (ready 2037) against a 2030 NGSA or 7-year fps (EIS 2037) is a pass with a note. Against a 10-year fps or fps via Embraer (2040) there are three years in hand. The order triggers only if UltraFan is ready by EIS, so nothing is compressed.
- Support: his concurrence rests on the support plan before EIS, carried here and in other_moves. If triggered: partner MRO shops on the Singapore joint-venture model near launch operators, with no own narrowbody MRO scale; repair technology developed alongside the test programme; a spares pool and field-service team for EIS; partner-shop agreements and castings, forgings and gearbox supply contracted with high-performing suppliers by the 2035 round; an EIS-readiness review before EIS. The test pacing is the full seven years: if a phase slips, the engine slips.
- Statement: the public statement gives no EIS earlier than launch + 7, no 2037 next to any airframe, and no airframer date. No veto stands. overrides is empty.

3. GRID, EACH ITEM AGAINST THE SAME ROW WITHOUT IT (S1/S2/S3/S4/S5/S6/S7/S8). Weights, confirmed by McCabe: S1 0.40, S2 0.05, S3 0.15, S4 0.03, S5 0.02, S6 0.10, S7 0.10, S8 0.15 (selection 0.10 in total, our rule for 'nothing on the record').
- ultrafan_nb_solo launch_if_selected ('UltraFan NB if selected' minus 'UltraFan NB: hold'): 0 / +32.60 / 0 / +28.24 / +44.54 / 0 / 0 / 0. Expected +3.37 (0.05x32.60 + 0.03x28.24 + 0.02x44.54). Board case (0.9 S1, 0.1 S2) +3.26; 0.1 on S4 alone +2.82. Worst column 0. Never below hold under any weights.
- Unconditional Solo instead, against the conditional: -8.00 in S1, S7 and S8, +3.57 in S3 and S6, expected -4.31. Against hold it is -0.94 expected, worst -8.00. Rejected: airframers first [RX-0058], the +$2B bar, McCabe's withheld signature and the Board veto.
- jv_with_pw commit, held ('if selected + commit to JV' minus 'if selected'): 0 everywhere except -4.00 in S7; expected -0.40. P&W has not committed, so a first commit is options management [RX-0051].
- ultrafan_wb launch, held ('if selected + UltraFan WB' minus 'if selected'): -4.00 in S1, S3, S6 and S7; -9.00 in S2, S4 and S5; -0.90 in S8; expected -4.04. No Re-engine is on the record, and the gap is above the $1B sub-cap.
- t1000_upgrade launch, held ('if selected + T1000 upgrade' minus 'if selected'): -0.98 untriggered, -5.98 in S2 and S4, -5.97 in S5, -0.29 in S8; expected -1.38. That is beyond its own $2B bill. Alone ('hold + T1000 upgrade' minus hold) it is -0.88 expected and -0.98 worst, and it would displace the conditional.

4. EXPECTED SCENARIO AND PREMIUM. I expect S1, rivals hold. In S1 the conditional and hold tie at +0.00, the best S1 plan. In expectation the conditional is the best row on the grid, at +3.37. Next come 'if selected + JV' +2.97, 'if selected + upgrade' +1.99, hold 0, 'if selected + UltraFan WB' -0.67 and Solo -0.94. The doctrine-favoured order is also the PV-best order: premium $0B.

5. RED LINES, AGAINST THE FINAL ORDERS. None breached. Both colleagues flagged option D (the upgrade beside launch_if_selected) as a red-line breach. It is struck: not ordered. There is no unconditional launch, no first Joint Venture commit and no UltraFan WB, and no item can lose more than its own bill (worst column 0). There is nothing to cancel.

6. CASH AS AN INPUT [RX-0042].
- Untriggered: £0.
- Triggered: $8B over 7 years, about $1.14B a year, about £0.84bn a year at 1.36 $/£ and about £5.9bn in total. That is 22-23% of FY2026 FCF guidance of £3.6-3.8bn [R-0222].
- Funding: from free cash flow, as redeployment inside a broadly flat R&D envelope [RX-0214]. It falls after the £7-9bn 2026-28 returns programme. No equity, and no leverage above about 1.5x.
- No widebody development runs beside it. If triggered, the upgrade waits until the 2045 round.

7. TRENT 1000 UPGRADE. My record backs regaining 787 share ('Absolutely' [RX-0101], 'Why not?' [RX-0117]). On this board, though, it earns nothing before 2042 without a Re-engine, and it cannot sit beside the conditional. So it is deferred, not dropped. I revisit it in 2035 if no UltraFan has triggered and a Re-engine is on the record, or as a declared premium within $3B. McCabe would co-sign it then.

8. DOCTRINE, NOT MY RECORD. My narrowbody launch record is Medium: words, no launch decision. The conditional form, the +$2B bar and the column weights are company doctrine and inference (profile.md §9; dashboard_game.md §5). The cash figures are McCabe's; readiness, strain and support are Watson's. Frankly, until I am sure we will deliver, I'm not committing: the conditional commits only when an airframer has chosen us and we can be ready by its EIS.

memo_weighing.cfo: Taken in full. McCabe confirmed my column weights, and her figures match mine: +3.37 expected, +3.26 on the Board's case, worst column 0. She co-signs launch_if_selected against the mid-to-high-teens hurdle. The selected columns are 3.5-5.6x the $8B bill. She gave capex a year if triggered (about £0.84bn, about £5.9bn in total, 22-23% of FY2026 FCF guidance), funded from FCF as redeployment, with no balance-sheet veto. She withholds her signature on E, F, G, C and D. I order none of them, so her binding vetoes are respected. I adopt her plan for failure (a 2035 cancel, $5.71B write-off, if the selecting airframe drops our code) and her Joint Venture timing (hold to 2035; formed then, ready in 2041). Premium confirmed at $0B. On the upgrade I take her answer: durability stays an other move, and she would co-sign the upgrade later as a declared premium with no UltraFan in play.
memo_weighing.ops: Taken in full. Watson finds the conditional ready by construction: zero margin against a 2030 NGSA or 7-year fps is a pass with a note, and a 10-year fps or fps via Embraer gives three years. His concurrence was conditional on the partner-shop support plan. I carry it in the rationale and as a private other move, so ground (c) does not arise. I take his statement advice: no 2037 next to any airframe, no airframer dates, and support through partner shops stated, not implied capability. I also drop 'we don't need partnership for capability' so it is not read as narrowbody MRO scale. I accept his strain call: nothing widebody while the conditional can trigger, and if it triggers the upgrade waits until the 2045 round. His capacity flag (a narrowbody ramp of about 800 engines a year against 197 widebody) is advice, not a veto. It goes into the 2035 supplier and MRO contracting. Widebody stays at 58%, about 53% under a GEnx upgrade, so nothing forces widebody spend now.

decision.expected_scenario: S1: rivals hold. No airframer launches a new narrowbody and no Re-engine is announced this round; P&W does not commit. It is the single most likely column, with weight 0.40.
decision.best_grid_plan_in_expected_scenario: In S1, 'UltraFan NB: hold' and 'UltraFan NB if selected' tie at +0.00, the best value in the column. 'UltraFan NB if selected' (launch_if_selected, all else hold) is therefore best in S1 and also best in expectation, at +3.37 over hold, because it adds +32.60 / +28.24 / +44.54 in S2, S4 and S5 at no cost elsewhere.
decision.premium_reason: None. The order doctrine favours ('UltraFan NB if selected', everything else at hold) is the best expected grid plan, at +3.37 against +2.97 for the next best ('if selected + JV'). There is no premium for the Trent 1000 upgrade (deferred, up to $0.98B not taken), for UltraFan WB (held; its gap is above the $1B sub-cap) or for narrowbody objective items (the Board allows none).
decision.objective_note:
Briefing goal: enter narrowbody, keep widebody dominance.

Widebody: met. RR stays at 58% in 2040, 2045 and 2050, with no widebody order. About 53% under a GEnx upgrade is still above 50%.

Narrowbody: met only if the conditional triggers (S2, S4, S5; weight 0.10). RR then has a narrowbody engine in service from 2037, so its share is above 0 in 2045 and 2050.

The unconditional Solo would also meet it in S3 and S6, through the +15 pp the board credits once any new narrowbody flies, lifting the probability to about 0.35. But that costs -4.31 expected against the conditional, is -8.00 in S1, S7 and S8, breaks the airframers-first red line and draws a Board veto. I pay no premium for the objective: 'We won't do anything not profitable.'

Route left for 2035: if no airframe selects us now, 2035 is the last round whose narrowbody launch can deliver by 2045. That could be a conditional against a 2035 airframe, or the Joint Venture if P&W's commitment is on the record (formed 2035, ready 2041).

recommendations.text: Public statement and other moves: publish the 'open door to Pratt & Whitney' move as openness only. Remove 'Formed then, the Joint Venture is ready in 2041' and any '2035' from its public text. Watson flagged this as a note, not a veto, because 2041 is formation + 6. Still, the Board would rather no ready date for any programme appeared in public before it is launched. Keep 2037 away from any airframe name.

If the conditional triggers, we want the following at the 2035 review. Watson's report on the partner-shop, castings, forgings and gearbox contracts. The status of gearbox sizing on the demonstrator, since that is the one thing that would turn the zero margin against a 2030 NGSA into a maturity concern. Confirmation that no test phase has been cut to hold 2037: if a phase slips, the engine slips.

If it triggers, McCabe should report the roughly £0.84bn a year (about £5.9bn over seven years) each round against a broadly flat R&D envelope and the post-2028 distribution plan, with leverage held at or below about 1.5x. Nothing widebody should run beside it: the Trent 1000 upgrade waits for the 2045 round and UltraFan WB stays at hold.
Plan for failure, as adopted: if a selecting airframe drops our code before EIS, bring the 2035 cancel ($8B x 5/7 = $5.71B write-off) rather than keep an orphan programme.

If nothing triggers in 2030, use the same conditional discipline in 2035, the last round whose narrowbody launch can deliver by 2045. Test the Joint Venture only once P&W's commitment is on the public record or a live airframe carries code 2, 4, 6 or 7, and only with a weighted value at or above 0 against the same row without it.

Widebody franchise: the test does not trigger (58% in 2040, 2045 and 2050; no Re-engine on the record). Watch for a rival-engined 787 Re-engine combined with a GEnx upgrade. In a round with no UltraFan in development or ordered, bring the Trent 1000 upgrade within our tests, either against a Re-engine on the record or as a declared premium inside $3B. Keep UltraFan WB at hold until a Re-engine is on the record.
Hold pricing discipline on any campaign: no concessions to buy narrowbody share, win-win terms, value remunerated. Narrowbody is an option, not a need.

Take Watson's capacity advice into the 2035 contracting. A narrowbody ramp of about 800 engines a year is about four times our 197 widebody engines a year on this board. It needs partner MRO and our high-performing suppliers, not capacity spread thin.

board_review.note: Product safety is and always must be our most important priority, and the balance sheet comes next. This package respects both. The one Board item, `ultrafan_nb_solo: launch_if_selected`, spends nothing unless an airframer names us and UltraFan can be ready by that aircraft's entry into service. It is 0 in every unselected column and +28.24 to +44.54 where we are selected. On McCabe's weights that is +3.37, on ours +3.26, and the worst case is 0 against an $8B bill. McCabe co-signs it. Watson invokes no Civil veto, and his support plan is carried in the orders. No premium is declared, and every hold stands. We approve. We do not want to underestimate the risks: zero margin against a 2030 NGSA, narrowbody support we have yet to build, and about £0.84bn a year if the order triggers. With these priorities set, the CEO has our total support.
